findings.F1: The test's result is near zero and on the side against the idea. The slope of the 30-day excess return on the forecast is -0.0076 with t -0.46 over 57 regime cases. The short-bet cases (forecast at or below -2) gained on average, +6.1 % excess over 30 days (n=16, t 0.91), where the idea says they should fall.
findings.F2: After an unusually large 90-day rise, coins kept rising rather than reversing. On the 30-bar grid, the regime cases' mean excess return was +7.3 % over 10 days (n=57, t 2.30), +5.5 % over 20 days (t 1.44) and +4.7 % over 30 days (t 0.88). The bars outside the regime had -1.7 % over 10 days (n=469, t -2.67).
findings.F3: A deeper volume drop was followed by a higher excess 30-day return, not a lower one. Where the 14-day/90-day volume ratio could be computed inside the regime, the slope of the excess 30-day return on the ratio was -0.163 (t -2.55, n=16). The highest-ratio tercile had -12.8 % against -0.1 % for the lowest, so the fading-volume short was on the wrong side.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 20-day return, the more its price moves further in the same direction over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean with a coin's recent month's move over the following ten days, and refuse to fade an extended rise on the grounds that its volume has faded.
ideas.name: short-horizon continuation after moves
